description: Shared, deliberate Renovate config committed byte-for-byte to all four 'ecosystem
bridge' orbs (bitrise, harness, bitbucket-pipes, buildkite). cci-labs/act is
intentionally excluded from this rollout -- it is on its own upgrade branch, handled
as a separate work stream, and never touched by this config.
Every non-default setting below carries its own "description" explaining why it
departs from config:recommended. Two things this config will NEVER do, by design:
(1) touch git tags, and (2) auto-merge anything -- these orbs are consumed by
customers, and each repo's own release-filters (tag regex /^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$/)
gates a real production orb publish (orb-tools/publish, pub_type: production). Renovate
only ever opens branches/PRs against a normal base branch and has no mechanism to push
a tag on its own, so this risk is structural, not just configured away -- but automerge
is disabled twice below (automerge + platformAutomerge) as defense in depth anyway.
Pinning vs. ranging: CircleCI orb references (namespace/orb@X.Y.Z) have no range syntax
at all -- every reference is already a single exact version, enforced by the platform.
Since these five orbs are themselves published for customers to depend on, treating our
own upstream pins (circleci/orb-tools, circleci/shellcheck) the same way -- one reviewed,
revertible commit per bump -- gives a clean paper trail from 'a production publish went
bad' back to 'this exact tooling bump'. We deliberately do NOT move any orb reference to
CircleCI's '@volatile' pseudo-version (always-latest, unpinned) even though Renovate
knows how to skip volatile orbs -- volatile would remove exactly the paper trail pinning
gives us. The same logic extends to Docker: every image already pinned to a real tag
(mvdan/shfmt, bitbucketpipelines/demo-pipe-bash, alpine in harness-orb's test fixture)
stays pinned to a real tag and Renovate bumps it like any other dependency. The only
images left unmanaged are CircleCI's own floating 'current' convenience tags
(cimg/base, the ubuntu-24.04 machine image) -- those are intentionally a moving target
maintained upstream, and 'local' tags built ad hoc inside a test job -- neither has a
'newer version' for Renovate to bump to.
Verified against Renovate's own docs before writing this (see PR/commit description
for links): the circleci manager scans any file matching /(^|/)\.circleci/.+\.ya?ml$/
and extracts both 'orb' and 'docker' datasource references from it -- so both
.circleci/config.yml and .circleci/test-deploy.yml are covered with zero extra config.
It does NOT reach into src/**/*.yml (orb source: executors, commands, jobs, examples) --
those either use a parameterised <<parameters.image>> (nothing concrete to bump) or are
illustrative example snippets referencing other companies' images for documentation
purposes only, never executed by this repo's own CI. We deliberately did not bolt on a
custom regex manager to reach into README.md/src/examples/*.yml: those pins are meant to
look like a plausible customer config, not track upstream, and Renovate silently
rewriting a docs example would be a worse outcome than leaving it alone.

vulnerabilityAlerts.description: Security-driven bumps should never sit in the queue for a weekly window -- let vulnerability-alert PRs raise immediately, on top of (not instead of) the normal weekly schedule everything else uses.

packageRules.description: Group this orb family's own CircleCI orb-tools/shellcheck version bumps into one PR, rather than one PR per orb -- a orb-tools bump changes the same lint/pack/review/continue pipeline every one of these repos shares, so reviewing them together (and running the one shared CI matrix once) is more useful than reviewing them apart.

Group every OTHER Docker image actually pinned to a real, resolvable tag -- across both the circleci manager (.circleci/config.yml's shfmt-check image, .circleci/test-deploy.yml's pinned vendor test-fixture images like bitbucketpipelines/demo-pipe-bash) and the dockerfile manager (harness-orb's test-fixtures/plugin/Dockerfile, currently 'FROM alpine:3.20') -- into one PR per digest/tag-bump cycle instead of a flood of one-image-at-a-time PRs. These are all test/tooling images with zero customer-facing blast radius, so grouping for review convenience costs nothing.
packageRules.groupName: docker image tag/digest updates (test + tooling images)

packageRules.description: Do NOT try to bump CircleCI's own floating 'current' convenience tags (cimg/base:current in every repo's shfmt/CLI-check jobs; the ubuntu-24.04 machine-executor image in harness-orb/bitbucket-pipes-orb/buildkite-orb's test-deploy.yml). 'current' is maintained and moved forward by CircleCI itself, on purpose, as the whole point of using it instead of a dated tag -- there is no 'newer current' for Renovate to open a PR for, and treating it as a version to pin would fight the reason these jobs use 'current' in the first place.

Do NOT try to resolve or bump ':local' image tags -- these are images built ad hoc inside a test job itself (bitbucket-pipes-orb's bitbucket-orb-test-pipe:local / bitbucket-orb-test-pipe-idempotency:local), never pushed to any registry Renovate could query. Leaving these unmatched would just generate a lookup-failure noise entry on the Dependency Dashboard for a 'dependency' that was never meant to be one.
